title: Cube of a rational number
competency: Calculate the cube of a number.

keywords.def: A number multiplied by itself three times: a³ = a × a × a.
A rational number x with x = m³ for some rational m, like 27 = 3³ or −64 = (−4)³.
Changing a number to a simpler, nearby value: look at the next digit; less than 5 round down, 5 or more round up.

en.text: Cubing means multiplying a number by itself three times: a³ = a × a × a. A negative number cubed stays negative, because three negative factors give a negative product. For a fraction, cube the top and the bottom.

am.text: ማኪዩብ ቁጥርን በራሱ ሦስት ጊዜ ማባዛት ነው፤ a³ = a × a × a። አሉታዊ ቁጥር ሲኪዩብ አሉታዊ ሆኖ ይቀራል።

screens.title: Building a cube
screens.ask: A box is filled with small cubes: 3 along, 3 across, 3 high. How many small cubes?
screens.after: 3 × 3 = 9 in one layer, and 3 layers: 9 × 3 = 27. This is 3 cubed, 3³.

screens.intro: A cube with sides of 3 small cubes. Build it one row, then one layer at a time.

screens.title: Cube numbers
paras: Definition 2.4: A cube number is a number multiplied by itself three times.
We write a × a × a as a³ and read it "a cubed".

screens.title: Square or cube?
screens.note: Move the slider. The cube grows much faster than the square: 10² = 100 but 10³ = 1000.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A number multiplied by itself three times: a³ = a × a × a.

screens.why:
2³ means 2 × 2 × 2 (three 2s).
2 × 2 = 4, then 4 × 2 = 8.
6 is 2 × 3: that is a common slip.

Sign: three negative factors → negative.
Tops: 1 × 1 × 1 = 1. Bottoms: 4 × 4 × 4 = 64.
So (−1/4)³ = −1/64.
screens.clue: Three negative factors: the answer is negative.

screens.ask: Volume of a cube = side × side × side. A cube has sides of 4 cm. Volume = ___ cm³
screens.why:
Volume = 4 × 4 × 4.
4 × 4 = 16, then 16 × 4 = 64.
So the volume is 64 cm³.
screens.clue: Volume of a cube = side × side × side.

screens.why:
(3/4)³ = (3 × 3 × 3)/(4 × 4 × 4).
Top: 27. Bottom: 64.
So (3/4)³ = 27/64, not 27/16. False: the bottom was squared, not cubed.

The answer is negative, so the number is negative (three negatives give a negative).
1 × 1 × 1 = 1 and 2 × 2 × 2 = 8.
So (−1/2)³ = −1/8.
screens.clue: Which fraction times itself three times gives −1/8? Think about the sign.

en.text: A perfect cube is a number you get by cubing a rational number: 1, 8, 27, −64, 1/8. Odd numbers in groups of 1, 2, 3, … add up to 1³, 2³, 3³, …: group n has n odd numbers, its middle number is n², so its sum is n × n² = n³. To estimate a cube, round first, then cube.

am.text: ፍጹም ኪዩብ ምክንያታዊ ቁጥርን በማኪዩብ የሚገኝ ቁጥር ነው። ቡድን n n ጎዶሎ ቁጥሮች አሉት፤ መካከለኛው n² ነው፤ ድምሩ n³ ነው።

screens.title: Group work 2.2
screens.after: 64 = 4³. Each group of odd numbers adds up to a cube! Build the groups below.

screens.title: Odd numbers in groups make cubes
The general pattern
paras: Group n has n odd numbers.
The numbers are evenly spaced, so their average is the middle number.
The middle number of group n is n × n = n².
So the sum of group n is n × n² = n³.
table: n numbers, starting at n² − n + 1
screens.note: The first number of group n is n² − n + 1. For n = 8: 64 − 8 + 1 = 57.

screens.title: Perfect cubes
paras: Definition 2.5: A rational number x is a perfect cube if x = m³ for some rational m.
A perfect cube is a product of three identical factors.
screens.note: To estimate a cube, round first: 3.2 ≈ 3, so (3.2)³ ≈ 27 (Example 2.16).

screens.title: Key words
defs: A rational number x with x = m³ for some rational m, like 27 = 3³ or −64 = (−4)³.

screens.text: Perfect cubes: which can be written as a number × itself × itself?
screens.clue: Can each be written as something × itself × itself?

screens.text: Is 144 a perfect cube? Compare it with the cubes near it.
screens.why:
5³ = 125 and 6³ = 216.
144 is between them, so no whole number cubed gives 144.
144 = 12², so it is a square, not a cube. (12³ = 1728.)
screens.clue: Find the cubes just below and above 144.

screens.ask: Estimate by rounding to a whole number: (4.98)³ ≈ ___
screens.why:
4.98 → the digit 9 is 5 or more → round up to 5.
5³ = 5 × 5 × 5 = 125.
So (4.98)³ ≈ 125 (exactly 123.505992).
screens.clue: Round to a whole number, then cube.
Work out each cube, then add.

screens.ask: Use the pattern: the next eight odd numbers after 55 add up to ___
screens.why:
They form group 8, so the sum is 8³.
Check the start: group 8 begins at 8² − 8 + 1 = 57.
The numbers are 57, 59, 61, 63, 65, 67, 69, 71. Their middle is 64 = 8².
Sum = 8 × 64 = 512 = 8³.
screens.clue: Group 8 has 8 numbers and its middle is 8².

items.text: Which number can be written as x³?
items.why:
729 = 9 × 9 × 9 = 9³.
121 = 11² is a square, not a cube.
2700 and 60 lie between cubes.

items.clue: Cube the top and the bottom.

items.ask: Estimate x³ by rounding: x = −3.45, so x³ ≈ ___
items.why:
−3.45 → the digit 4 is less than 5 → round to −3.
(−3)³ = −27.

notes.text: The competency lines of 2.2.1 (cube) and 2.2.2 (cube root) appear swapped in the book. The lessons use the matching competency.
Exercise 2.6 Q3: rounding to a whole number gives rough estimates far from the exact cubes for a, c, d (e.g. (2.75)³ = 20.80 but ≈ 27). Kept as the book's method.
v2 (2026-10-24): odd-number cube groups with the general rule (middle = n², sum = n³), square-vs-cube slider (owner feedback).

screens.title: Round 4.3 and 2.45
screens.text: Look at the next digit to the right.
steps: 4.3 to a whole number: the next digit is 3. 3 < 5, so round down: 4.
2.45 to one decimal place: the next digit is 5. 5 or more, so round up: 2.5.

screens.text: Round 10.8 to the nearest whole number.
screens.why:
Look at the digit after the point: 8.
8 is 5 or more, so round up.
10.8 → 11.
screens.clue: Is the digit after the point less than 5?
